title: Inlet Thermistor Open Circuit
shortDescription: The inlet temperature thermistor has an open circuit, preventing temperature monitoring.
fullDescription: Error code E4A indicates the inlet (supply air) temperature thermistor has failed with an open circuit condition. The control board cannot read the air temperature entering the drum, which is essential for proper heat regulation. The dryer will stop to prevent overheating.

causes.cause: Control board thermistor input circuit failure

symptoms: Dryer will not start or stops mid-cycle

fixSteps.title: Locate the inlet thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer. The inlet thermistor is typically located near the heating element housing or at the air intake duct. Consult your model's wiring diagram for exact location.

fixSteps.title: Check wiring connection
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the thermistor wire connector for looseness or corrosion. Disconnect and reseat the connector firmly.

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the thermistor leads. Measure resistance with a multimeter. At room temperature (72F/22C), it should read approximately 10K-12K ohms. An open reading (infinite/OL) confirms the thermistor is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the mounting screw or clip holding the thermistor. Install the new thermistor in the same location and reconnect the wiring.

whenToCallPro: Only if replacing the thermistor does not resolve the error, suggesting a control board issue.

shortDescription: The exhaust temperature thermistor has failed or is reading out of range.

symptoms: Dryer runs but does not dry clothes properly

fixSteps.title: Test thermistor resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the thermistor and measure resistance. At room temperature, expect 10K-12K ohms. If the reading is open (OL) or zero, the thermistor is faulty.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the old thermistor and install the replacement. Ensure proper routing of wires away from heat sources.

fixSteps.instruction: Test the high-limit thermostat for continuity. If open, it has tripped and needs replacement. Also investigate why it tripped (usually restricted airflow).

fixSteps.title: Test heating element
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the heating element leads. Measure resistance across the element terminals. Should read 8-20 ohms for electric dryers. An open reading means the element has burned out.

title: Water Leak Detected (E13)
shortDescription: The Frigidaire dryer reports E13 indicating a fault in the leak sensor, which prevents the cycle from completing safely.
fullDescription: Error code E13 on a Frigidaire dryer indicates the control board has detected an abnormal condition involving the leak sensor. The board interrupts the running cycle to prevent damage to the appliance, the laundry load, or surrounding wiring. The dryer logs the fault, locks out further operation until power is cycled, and surfaces the E13 banner to alert the user. Although the immediate trigger is the leak sensor, the underlying cause can range from a damaged wiring harness, to an aged sensor returning out-of-spec readings, to a failed relay on the main control board itself. Diagnosis should always begin with the simplest possible cause (loose connectors, lint blockage, recent power events) before escalating to component replacement.

causes.cause: Leak sensor wiring harness loose or chafed
Leak sensor component reached end of service life and is out of spec
Recent power surge or brownout corrupted control board state
Main control board relay or driver circuit has failed

symptoms: Error code E13 flashes on the display
Cycle stops before clothes are dry
Dryer refuses to start a new cycle
Audible beep or chime accompanies the error

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the dryer
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer from the wall outlet, or switch off the dedicated breaker, for at least five full minutes. This forces the control board to dump any latched fault states. Restore power and start a short timed-dry cycle to confirm whether the E13 error returns.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the leak sensor
fixSteps.instruction: With the dryer unplugged, access the leak sensor per your model's service sheet. Visually inspect for burnt or melted insulation, loose spade connectors, lint build-up, and signs of moisture. Reseat every connector you find and confirm the ground path is intact.

fixSteps.title: Test the leak sensor with a multimeter
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the leak sensor from the harness and measure resistance or continuity across its terminals. Compare the reading against the value on the model's tech sheet. If the part reads open, shorted, or far outside the documented range, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Replace the leak sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Order a model-specific leak sensor from an authorized parts supplier. Install the new part using the original mounting hardware, route the harness clear of hot surfaces and moving components, and reassemble the dryer. Run a full timed cycle to confirm the fault clears.

whenToCallPro: If replacing the leak sensor does not clear the E13 error, or if you find evidence of burnt traces on the main control board, schedule a certified appliance technician. Internal PCB repair, refrigerant work (heat-pump models), and any 240 V wiring inside the cabinet should not be attempted by a DIYer without the correct training and tooling.

faq.q: Can I keep using the dryer with E13 showing?
faq.a: No - the control board has shut the cycle down for safety. Diagnose and resolve the fault before further use.

faq.q: Will a power cycle permanently clear E13?
faq.a: Only if the trigger was a transient glitch. If the underlying part is failing, the error will return within a few cycles.

faq.q: Is this code covered under warranty?
faq.a: Most major brands cover the main control board for 1 year and sealed-system parts (heat pump) for longer - check your specific warranty card.
